reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification, in order.

0001 (construction): Heawood graph = Fano incidence graph, Aut = PGL(2,7) of order 336, with the part-preserving subgroup PSL(2,7) = PGL(3,2) of index 2. Adding a 7-clique on the point side makes point-vertices degree 3+6=9 and line-vertices degree 3, so every automorphism preserves the bipartition; cross-part edges are exactly the incidences and within-part edges exactly the clique, so Aut of the new 14-vertex graph is exactly the Fano collineation group PGL(3,2) = PSL(2,7). Justified.

0007-0013 (Fano restatement): identical graph; the clique breaks point-line duality. Justified.

0017 (lower bound 7 and exclusion of n=7): PSL(2,7) has minimal faithful degree 7, and any degree-7 faithful action has point stabilizer of index 7 (order 24, S4), which is 2-transitive; a graph invariant under a 2-transitive group is complete or empty, whose group is S7. So n=7 is impossible independently of the cited 1044-graph computation. Justified.

0019: |Aut| = 168 gives an order-7 element by Cauchy; its orbits have size 1 or 7 and n <= 13 < 14 forces exactly one 7-orbit A. PSL(2,7) is simple so n_7 = 8, giving tau of order 7 outside <sigma>. Justified.

0021: sigma fixes everything off A, tau everything off B, so both fix any v outside A u B; since n <= 13, A n B is nonempty, hence A u B is <sigma,tau>-invariant and a single orbit, giving the all-or-none adjacency of v to A u B, and hence the extension property Aut(G[A u B]) -> Aut(G). Justified.

0025 (Case A = B): contains one literal misstatement: a subgroup of S7 generated by two 7-cycles lies in A7 (7-cycles are even), so it can never be S7; the omitted possibility is A7, realized by suitable pairs of 7-cycles. This does not break the step: the dismissal used is 'too many automorphisms', and |A7| = 2520 does not divide 168, so A7 is excluded by exactly the reason given for the third case. The trichotomy that the argument actually needs (C7, PSL(2,7), or something of order > 168) holds, so <sigma,tau> = Aut(G) = PSL(2,7). Repairable in place; not a genuine gap.

0027: Aut(G) = <sigma,tau> fixes all vertices off A, so restriction to G[A] is injective, and 0021 gives surjectivity onto Aut(G[A]); hence a 7-vertex graph with group PSL(2,7), contradicting 0017. Justified.

0031 (Case A != B): v in A\B, w in B\A exist; complementation is harmless since Aut(G) = Aut(complement) and A, B stay orbits. tau fixes v and is transitive on B, so v is joined to all of B. The stated route via sigma is loose (sigma^k(B) = sigma^k(A n B) u (B\A), not B), but the asserted conclusion is correct by the symmetric one-line argument: sigma fixes w, so w is joined to all of A, and then tau^k gives every vertex of B joined to all of A\B.

0033: with A = Z7 and sigma = +1, S = A n B a nonempty proper subset, the difference set (A\S) - S is all of Z7\{0} (if S + d = S for d != 0 then S is a union of cosets of <d> = Z7), so translating the complete bipartite A\B to A n B pattern gives every edge inside A; symmetrically inside B, and A x (B\A), (A\B) x B are already complete. So G[A u B] is complete. Justified.

0035: |A u B| >= 8, so at least 8! automorphisms of H, all extending to G by 0021, contradicting |Aut(G)| = 168. Justified.

No step fails definitively; the only defects are the S7/A7 slip in 0025 and the loose transport in 0031, both of which have immediate corrections that leave every stated conclusion intact. Verdict VALID.
